claims.text: The driver's own GPS trace never brings him anywhere near the pickup pin. Across 49 fixes his closest approach is 177.53 m from the pin, with a mean of 180.78 m and a maximum of 184.39 m, against a 120 m arrival radius for a LARGE_VENUE pickup such as The Cascadia guardhouse. On the POL-NS-02 proximity test there is not one admissible in-radius fix, so the driver never arrived.

Because the driver never entered the geofence, POL-NS-01 fails at limb (b) (no in-geofence fix at or before the 'arrived' event) and again at limb (c): the trace records 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds against the 300-second minimum dwell for LARGE_VENUE. The clause is conjunctive and requires all four conditions; breaking one is enough, and two are broken.

The dwell shortfall is total rather than marginal: effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against a required 300 seconds, a shortfall of 300 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 a dwell shorter than the zone minimum means the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages.

In the alternative the facts sit squarely inside POL-NS-03's wrong-entrance band. The driver held position at roughly 180 m from the pin for the whole waiting window (speeds between 0.0 and 2.3 kph) — outside the 120 m arrival radius but well inside the 400 m ceiling that is the whole test — so POL-NS-03 refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full on the same basis as POL-NS-02.

No driver compensation attaches under POL-NS-03. Fault is allocated from the chat log for compensation only, and limb (i) applies: the rider named the meeting point in the chat log — 'pin is the guardhouse where every driver stops. please come in' — and the driver never moved to it before cancelling at 09:23:50. Limb (ii) cannot apply either, because the trip records only 1 registered pickup point, not 2 or more, so there is no pin-ambiguity goodwill to pay.

The rider did everything the platform asks of her. Her device track is available and places her within 10.24 m of the pin at her furthest, across 42 qualifying fixes spanning the whole waiting window, against a 150 m rider-presence radius for LARGE_VENUE. She was at the guardhouse; this is not a rider who failed to show.

I will not stretch POL-NS-04, and it does not carry this case. Limbs (a) and (c) are met — the rider sent a coordinating message at 09:20:20 and was inside the presence radius — but limb (b) is defeated, because the driver placed an in-app voice call at 09:18:40, answered for 65 seconds, before terminating the trip. The rider therefore rests on the geofence failure under POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02, POL-NS-03 and POL-NS-06, none of which depends on POL-NS-04.

The driver's 'your pin wrong' defence — repeated in his chat message and his filed statement — is not supported by the record. The trip's own pickup label is 'The Cascadia, 305 Bukit Timah Rd (Guardhouse)', the trip records a single registered pickup point, and the rider's chat identifies the guardhouse as the meeting point. Nothing in the evidence establishes a second entrance or face of the building he was entitled to hold at.

There is no traffic advisory covering this pickup road: EV-ADVIS-00620-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0. POL-NS-06 limb (i) requires a present and populated advisory of an admissible type before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed, so no accumulation is available and the 0-second dwell stands unimpeached.

Compensation to the driver is not payable. POL-NS-07 compensates only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not satisfied on any limb (b), (c) or (d). For completeness, the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check would not bite in any event: 1 no-show termination in 30 days against 110 completed trips is far below the 4-termination and 0.08-rate thresholds, so no escalation is triggered on that limb.

The amount to be returned is the full SGD 4.00 cancellation fee. The fare ledger shows a 4.00 cancellation_fee line, which reconciles with the fee schedule's greater-of test for this trip (LARGE_VENUE zone fee 4.00 and RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee 4.00 both produce 4.00). There is no fare defect under POL-NS-08(d) and no basis to discount the refund; the rider has paid it (payment_status CHARGED) and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00.

Nothing in this record requires escalation under POL-NS-09. No limb (a)-(d) impairment under POL-NS-08 is present (no clock skew, no sampling gap over 120 seconds, no chat defect, fare reconciles), the parties have 0 prior no-show disputes with each other in 90 days, the rider has 0 no-show disputes in 30 days, and the deciding facts rest on complete weight-1.0 telemetry. The case is decidable now, on a full refund.

claims.text: The rider's exoneration route under POL-NS-04 fails at limb (b). Her only locating message was sent at 09:20:20, but the driver had already placed a 65-second in-app voice call at 09:18:40 which the rider answered, and that call is recorded in trip_record.in_app_calls before the 09:23:50 cancellation. Limb (b) requires that the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor placed an in-app call at any point before terminating the trip; the recorded call defeats it, so POL-NS-04 does not apply and the residual mislocation is dealt with under POL-NS-03.

There is no false arrival marker here, and the rider cannot obtain one. At the 09:17:52 arrival event the driver's own trace places him between 177.5 m and 184.4 m from the pin - well inside the 300 m ceiling - while travelling at 0.0 to 2.3 kph, far below the 15 kph motion trigger. POL-NS-05 is not engaged, no false-arrival referral is available against this driver, and the case is a POL-NS-03 wrong-entrance matter.

The driver did not abandon the pickup. His trace is 100 percent covered, 49 fixes with no gap and no interval longer than the 10 second cadence, and it shows a continuous essentially stationary hold from 09:15:40 to 09:23:40 - about 480 seconds - at a mean of 180.8 m from the pin, squarely inside POL-NS-03's 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling. On POL-NS-03's own terms this is a wrong-face-of-the-venue case, not a driver who was never at the venue; the geofence failure is a POL-NS-03 question and not evidence of desertion.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming branch is not triggered. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by 110 completed trips is 0.009, far below the 0.08 rate cap. Both limbs must hold, so neither does: the driver's fee is not withheld on this ground and POL-NS-09(d) does not escalate this case for driver-side abuse.

On POL-NS-03's fault allocation, limb (i) is not made out, so the loss is not laid at the driver's door. The pickup label already reads 'The Cascadia, 305 Bukit Timah Rd (Guardhouse)', and the rider's only message merely restated that same pin - 'pin is the guardhouse where every driver stops. please come in' - naming no entrance, block or tower beyond the label the driver already had. The rider supplied no sub-location that the driver failed to move to.

ruling.explanation: Both parties: the SGD 4.00 no-show cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full. The driver never reached the pickup pin. His own GPS trace (EV-GPS-00620, 49 fixes, no gaps, 10 s cadence) places him between 177.5 m and 184.4 m from the pin for the whole waiting window 09:15:40 to 09:23:40, and never inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup (The Cascadia guardhouse). Under POL-NS-02 there is not one admissible in-radius fix, so the driver is not deemed to have arrived, and POL-NS-01 fails at limb (b) and again at limb (c): the trace records 0 in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying dwell of 0.0 s against the 300 s minimum. Because the driver was nonetheless stationary for a continuous 480 s at about 180 m from the pin - outside the 120 m radius but well inside the 400 m ceiling - POL-NS-03 governs, its distance test is met, and it refunds the cancellation fee in full. POL-NS-06 reaches the same result independently: effective in-geofence dwell of 0 s against 300 s required is a 300 s shortfall, and the fee is not chargeable. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00620-01, weight 0.0) is why separate in-geofence intervals cannot be summed and seconds cannot be accumulated, but here there are none to sum. On the driver's points: I accept the arrival marker was not false - at 09:17:52 he was about 180 m from the pin, under the 300 m trigger, and moving at 0.0-2.3 kph, under the 15 kph trigger - so POL-NS-05 is not engaged and no false-arrival referral is made. I accept POL-NS-04 does not carry the rider: her coordinating message at 09:20:20 was preceded by the driver's answered 65-second in-app call at 09:18:40, which defeats limb (b). I accept the anti-farming check does not bite (1 no-show termination against 110 completed trips), so POL-NS-09(d) does not escalate. But none of this helps the driver, because his own trace defeats the fee under POL-NS-02, POL-NS-03 and POL-NS-06. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not. Under POL-NS-03 the trip records a single registered pickup point, so the pin-ambiguity goodwill is unavailable, and the rider did identify the guardhouse as the meeting point, so the loss sits with the driver; his 'wrong pin' account in chat and in his filed statement is not supported by the record. Deciding facts rest on the GPS trace and trip record, both weight 1.0, and no POL-NS-08 impairment applies - no clock skew, no trace gap, no chat defect, and the 4.00 fee reconciles with the greater-of test (LARGE_VENUE 4.00, RYDE_X 4.00) - so the case is decidable without escalation. The full 4.00 charged is returned; refund_issued_sgd remains 0.00 until processed.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to you in full. To the driver: the fee you charged does not stand, and no compensation is payable to you.

What the record shows. The driver's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-00620, weight 1.0) runs 100 percent covered, 49 fixes at 10-second cadence with no gap, and places the vehicle at a minimum of 177.53 m, a mean of 180.78 m and a maximum of 184.39 m from the pickup pin for the whole 09:15:40 to 09:23:40 window, at speeds of 0.0 to 2.3 km/h. The pickup is a LARGE_VENUE (The Cascadia, 305 Bukit Timah Rd (Guardhouse)), so the arrival radius is 120 m and the required dwell is 300 seconds.

Why the fee falls. POL-NS-01 is conjunctive. Limb (b) fails because the trace contains no in-radius fix at or before the 09:17:52 'arrived' event, and limb (c) fails because the trace records 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds against the 300-second minimum. POL-NS-02 then finds no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the 15 minutes before cancellation, so the driver never arrived. Because he was nonetheless stationary for the required dwell at about 180 m from the pin — outside the 120 m radius but well inside the 400 m ceiling that is the whole test — POL-NS-03 governs the outcome and refunds the cancellation fee in full. POL-NS-06 reaches the same result independently: effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against a 300-second minimum, a 300-second shortfall, and a shortfall refunds the fee whether or not the rider was present. The amount is read off the fare ledger (EV-FARE-00620): a cancellation_fee of SGD 4.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The SGD 4.00 reconciles with the fee schedule's greater-of test, since the LARGE_VENUE zone fee of SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of SGD 4.00 are equal, so there is no defect under POL-NS-08(d) and no discount to the refund.

On compensation. Fault is allocated from the chat log under POL-NS-03 for compensation only. The rider's message of 09:20:20 named the guardhouse as the meeting point, and the driver did not move to it before cancelling at 09:23:50. Limb (ii) cannot apply in any event: trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 1, not 2 or more. Either way the driver receives nothing, and the two advocate claims on this point — the driver's that limb (i) is not made out, and the rider's that limb (i) applies — are answered together: both roads lead to no compensation.

The rider's POL-NS-04 route does not carry the case, and both sides correctly concede it. The rider's limbs (a) and (c) are met — her device track (EV-GPS-00620) sits within 10.24 m of the pin across 42 qualifying fixes against a 150 m radius, and she sent a coordinating message at 09:20:20 — but limb (b) is defeated by the driver's 65-second answered in-app call placed at 09:18:40 and recorded in trip_record.in_app_calls (EV-TRIP-00620) before termination. POL-NS-04 therefore does not apply, and the rider wins on the geofence and dwell failures instead, which depend on none of it. That route reaches the same full refund.

Claims that could have changed the outcome but do not. POL-NS-05 is not engaged: at the 09:17:52 marker the driver was roughly 180 m from the pin, under the 300 m ceiling, and stationary, so the arrival marker is not false and no false-arrival referral arises in the driver's favour or against him. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip — no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against a threshold of 4, and 1 of 110 completed trips is 0.009 against a rate cap of 0.08 — so no escalation and no compensation arise there either. The driver's 'your pin wrong' defence is not made out on this record: the pickup label itself reads '(Guardhouse)', the trip records a single registered pickup point, and nothing in the evidence establishes a second entrance or face of the building that the driver was entitled to hold at.

No escalation and no referral. Confidence rests on artifacts at weight 1.0 throughout and stands above the 0.70 floor. No two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; the parties have 0 prior no-show disputes with each other in 90 days and the rider has 0 no-show disputes in 30 days; there is no POL-NS-08(a)-(d) impairment — clock skew is about 2 seconds between the arrival event and the nearest fix, there is no sampling gap, the two chat messages match chat_message_count of 2, and the fare reconciles. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00620-01 is absent (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), but nothing turns on it: because there is no in-geofence interval, POL-NS-06 limb (i) accumulation has nothing to sum, and no limb of the ruling rests on it. No clause in the loaded policy produces a referral, so the referrals list is empty.

One open matter, which belongs here rather than in a referral: the rider's account of the phone call and the driver's counter-account of who was rude are not decidable from this record and are not the subject of the fee. Either party may raise conduct through the platform's support channel.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: this was a failed pickup at The Cascadia (Guardhouse) on 20 September 2026, and the only question is whether the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee charged on EV-FARE-00620 (cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) can stand. It cannot, and the whole SGD 4.00 is refunded to the rider.

The pickup is a LARGE_VENUE zone, so the driver had to be inside 120 m of the pin (EV-GPS-00620 thresholds) and then hold there for 300 continuous seconds (POL-NS-01(c), fee_schedule). His own trace — 49 fixes, full 100% coverage, no gap, 10-second cadence — puts his closest approach at 177.53 m, mean 180.78 m, maximum 184.39 m. He never entered the arrival radius at all, and the in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against 300 required, a shortfall of 300 seconds. POL-NS-01 limb (b) and limb (c) both fail, so the fee is not chargeable under the anchor clause.

Because the driver was nonetheless stationary (speeds 0.0–2.3 kph) for well over the required dwell, roughly 09:15:40 to 09:23:40 at about 180 m from the pin, this is a POL-NS-03 wrong-entrance case and not a POL-NS-05 false-arrival case: his hold is inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, so POL-NS-02 yields to POL-NS-03, which refunds the fee in full. POL-NS-06 arrives at the same result on the 300-second shortfall. Rider claims on the geofence failure (POL-NS-02, POL-NS-01 limbs (b)/(c), POL-NS-03, POL-NS-06) are accepted; they agree with each other and all point to the full refund.

Driver compensation: none. POL-NS-07 compensates only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not satisfied on limbs (b), (c) or (d). POL-NS-03 pays the 50% pin-ambiguity goodwill (SGD 2.00) only where limb (ii) applies, which requires two or more registered pickup points; this trip registers exactly one. On limb (i): the rider's chat message ('pin is the guardhouse where every driver stops. please come in') names the meeting point and asks the driver in, and the driver never moved to it before cancelling at 09:23:50, so the loss stays with the driver. I have read the driver's contrary argument that the rider merely restated the pin's own label, but even on that reading limb (ii) still cannot bite (one registered pickup point), so no compensation is payable either way. The driver's filed statement ('I stopped at the main road like always') does not change this, and it carries no weight of its own.

On the driver's other points, all accepted: the 65-second in-app call at 09:18:40 defeats POL-NS-04 limb (b), so the rider's own exoneration clause does not apply and her refund rests on the geofence failure, not on POL-NS-04; and the arrival marker is not false (177 m, stationary, far under the 300 m and 15 kph triggers of POL-NS-05), so no false-arrival referral is recorded against the driver. His anti-farming answer is also correct: 1 no-show termination in 30 days against 110 completed trips is below the 4-termination and 0.08-rate thresholds, so POL-NS-07 and POL-NS-09(d) do not bite and no driver-side abuse escalation arises.

Escalation is not required. ruling.explanation: To both parties. The sum in dispute is the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee itemised in the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00620). It reconciles with the fee schedule: this is a LARGE_VENUE pickup with a RYDE_X vehicle, and both the zone-class fee and the vehicle-tier fee are SGD 4.00, so the greater-of figure is SGD 4.00. That fee is refunded to the rider in full. The baseline no-show clause, POL-NS-01, is not satisfied. Limb (b) requires the driver's own GPS trace to place him inside the pickup geofence before his 'arrived' event. The pickup is The Cascadia guardhouse, a LARGE_VENUE site, so the arrival radius is 120 m; the driver's trace (EV-GPS-00620) never brings him closer than 177.53 m to the pin (mean 180.78 m, maximum 184.39 m over 49 fixes), so there is no in-radius fix at all. Limb (c) also fails: effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 300-second minimum for LARGE_VENUE. POL-NS-01 is conjunctive, so the fee is not chargeable under it, and no driver compensation follows from it. Because the driver was nonetheless stationary for the required 300 seconds at a point outside the 120 m radius but within 400 m of the pin — his trace holds from 09:15:40 to 09:23:40, about 480 seconds, at roughly 180 m, at speeds of 0.0 to 2.3 kph — POL-NS-03 governs, exactly as POL-NS-02 says it must. Under POL-NS-03 the driver did not arrive at the pickup point and the cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full. POL-NS-06 points the same way: 0 seconds of dwell against a 300-second minimum is a 300-second shortfall, and the fee is not chargeable. There is no driver compensation. POL-NS-03 pays a platform-funded goodwill of 50 percent of the fee only where neither party specified a sub-location and the trip records 2 or more registered pickup points; this trip records 1 (EV-TRIP-00620), so limb (ii) cannot apply. In any event the rider did name the meeting point in the chat log ('pin is the guardhouse where every driver stops. please come in', 09:20:20) and the driver did not move to it before cancelling at 09:23:50, so under limb (i) the loss would fall on the driver. The rider's POL-NS-04 route does not carry the case, as the rider accepts: the rider's own track places her within 10.24 m of the pin across the whole window (150 m presence radius for LARGE_VENUE), but the driver placed and the rider answered a 65-second in-app call at 09:18:40, which defeats limb (b). Nothing turns on this, because the refund rests on the geofence failure, not on POL-NS-04. The driver's defence that the pin was wrong is not made out, and POL-NS-05 is not engaged: at the 09:17:52 arrival event the driver was 177 to 184 m from the pin, inside POL-NS-05's 300 m trigger, and travelling at 0.0 to 2.3 kph, far below the 15 kph motion trigger. The arrival marker is therefore not a false-arrival event, no false-arrival referral arises, and this is the wrong-entrance situation POL-NS-03 describes — a driver at the venue but at the wrong face of it, not one who was never there. The pickup label names the guardhouse and the rider identified herself as at the guardhouse; nothing in the record establishes a second, equally valid pickup point the driver was entitled to hold at. No escalation arises under POL-NS-09. The GPS trace is complete (100 percent coverage, 49 fixes, no gap), the trip record and trace agree on timing (arrival 09:17:52 against a 10-second fix cadence) and on the chat count, and the fare reconciles, so POL-NS-08 is not engaged on any limb. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check is not tripped (1 no-show termination in 30 days against 110 completed trips, a rate of 0.009, below both thresholds, and both limbs are required), and the parties have no prior no-show disputes with each other in 90 days. Confidence is 0.95. One open question is noted but is not a referral: the rider reports the driver was rude on the call and used abusive language, and the driver says the rider was rude first. No clause in this category produces a conduct referral, so none is added; the platform may wish to review the call recording independently.
